**Allowed origins** are set by the `origin` callback passed to `cors({...})` in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. It's registered with `app.use('*', ...)`, so it covers every route. It returns the request's origin if one of these is true, and `null` (blocked) otherwise:
- `origin === 'http://localhost:4200'` (exact match)
- `origin.endsWith('.pages.dev')`
- `origin.endsWith('.workers.dev')`

Requests with no `Origin` header also get `null`, from `if (!origin) return null;`.

Other CORS settings in the same block:
- `allowMethods`: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS
- `allowHeaders`: Content-Type, Authorization
- `maxAge`: 86400

**Adding a custom domain:** edit the `if (...)` condition inside that `origin` function, at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. Add one more `||` clause.
- For one exact domain, add `origin === 'https://app.example.com' ||`.
- For a wildcard subdomain, add `origin.endsWith('.example.com') ||`.

Don't add the domain to an array form of `origin`. Hono matches array entries as exact strings, and the code comment at line 20 says so. `worker/src/index.md:24-25` says the same, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 covers CORS.

`endsWith('.example.com')` would also match `https://evil.example.com`, so only use it for domains you control. The existing `.pages.dev` and `.workers.dev` checks already allow any account's subdomain on those hosts. That's looser than it looks. I didn't read DEPLOYMENT_NOTES §4, so I can't say whether it addresses this.

After the edit, redeploy the Worker. I didn't check whether the frontend's API base URL also needs changing for the new domain. The doc for that is `frontend/src/app/services/game-api.service.md`.
